shared_elements: carved stone surface in low relief
net/grid pattern of crossing incised lines
rows of short parallel incised strokes forming a band
justification: The one specific correspondence is the band of crossing incised lines forming a net or grid of lozenges, which appears as a horizontal register across the flat face in A and as a curving woven-looking field wrapping the lump in B. Otherwise they differ fundamentally: A is a large flat panel dominated by figural low relief (birds, quadrupeds, discs, a human-like figure) arranged in stacked registers, while B is a small three-dimensional, roughly rounded object with no identifiable figures and no register structure.
